attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses this assessment in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the descriptive assessment and the material hedge about enforcement adequacy. The observation includes an unscorable policy judgment.

contract.note: The contract fairly interprets breadth and mandatory authority while recognising that Marcus supplies no adequacy threshold. Its plain-reading provision cannot make the hedged judgment scorable.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous government announcement documents scope and mandatory reporting. It informs the descriptive components but cannot establish overall adequacy; its safety assurances are not independent findings.

reviews.rationale: The complete claim materially includes a probabilistic judgment about whether enforcement powers are sufficient. Policy excludes that hedge from scoring, and no reproducible adequacy standard is supplied. Mandatory reporting neither settles adequacy nor supports the complete proposition.
